descriptionAdvanced.en: Abomey-Calavi, located in the Atlantique Department, serves as a crucial urban center just north of Cotonou. Once a smaller settlement, it has exploded into one of Benin's most populous urban areas due to its proximity to the economic capital. The city is home to the University of Abomey-Calavi, the largest and most prestigious academic institution in the nation, which attracts students from across West Africa. Its rapid expansion has transformed it into a vital residential and administrative hub, connecting the vibrant coastal economy with the country's interior. Geography K7 — urban development and regional growth.

en: Population growth accelerated significantly after the year 2000.
The university was established in 1970 as the University of Dahomey.
Abomey-Calavi acts as a primary dormitory suburb for the Cotonou workforce.
It is situated at an elevation of approximately 30 meters above sea level.
The city covers a vast area that bridges coastal lagoons and inland plateaus.
Benin's population density is highest in the southern urban corridor including Abomey-Calavi.
